newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students confess to beating death.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students confess to beating death.

text.p: Militant South Korean left-wing students on Wednesday took responsibility for the death of a man they severely beat as a suspected police informer during an interrogation.
A leader of the outlawed Hanchongryon group told a news conference the victim had died in his sleep after being beaten by students at Hanyang University during the night.

"We are ready to take full responsibility," said Lee Jun-ook, who appeared at the news conference dressed in a black suit and black tie. His group is branded by the South Korean government as a stooge of rival North Korea.
"We are ready to cooperate with police so long as a fair investigation is promised," the leader said.
Earlier, a police official identified the man as Lee Suk, 22, an office worker from Suwon. The official denied the man was a police informer.

The Hanchongryon leader said the victim had tried to strangle his student interrogator in a room in the student union building. Other students burst into the room to intervene, bound the man's wrists and beat him.
During his interrogation, the man signed a confession that he was an informer, the student leader said.
The man spent the night in a room with two students, who found him lifeless in the morning, the student leader said. He was taken to the Hanyang University hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
The police official said the corpse was covered in bruises when it was delivered to the hospital by students, who immediately fled.

Over the past several days, Hanyang has been the scene of violent clashes between riot police and rock-throwing students led by Hanchongryon, which has been trying to stage a campus ceremony to inuagurate new office holders.
A police office died during clashes outside the campus on Monday. An autopsy on Tuesday found he probably died after being run over by a police vehicle, not at the hands of militant students.
Violence associated with the Hanchongryon inauguration ceremonies has merged into wider student agitation to demand the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
Several hundred radical students are holed up on the campus, and the student leader called on police to let them return home, while promising to indefinitely postpone the Hanchongryon ceremonies.
"We ask that police not crack down on Hanchongryon over this incident," he said. Students were ready to fight if police tried to raid the campus.
Senior prosecutor Shin Gun-soo said police would investigate the incident. "The incident has proved the violent nature of the Hanchongryon," he said.
A total of 151 Hanchongryon leaders have been arrested since the last round of campus violence in August last year.

President Kim Young-sam had demanded a thorough investigation into the earlier death of the riot policeman and threatened "severe punishment" for those responsible. This followed an order by state prosecutors for a further roundup of Hanchongryon leaders.
Since student unrest began on Friday, 215 police officers have been injured, 40 severely, according to police figures. A total of 34 students have been arrested.
One student is recovering from brain surgery after being injured in hand-to-hand combat on a bridge leading to Hanyang University on Monday.
